title: Pink Ballerina Halloween Costume You Can Rewear
intro: A pink ballerina costume that does not live in a bin after October. The tutu is the fun part, but the wrap top, tights and satin flats are real wardrobe pieces. I wore it with leg warmers and an iced coffee, obviously.

sections.heading: Start with the wrap top, not the tutu
paragraphs: Everyone shops the tutu first. I get it, it is the fun part. But the long sleeve ballet wrap top is what makes this read grown-up ballerina instead of recital at age six. In the flat lay you can see how it crosses at the front and ties at the waist, with a little white tank peeking out underneath. That tank is a good idea if the V runs deeper than you want.

In the lifestyle photo I tied it off to one side so the knot sits right on the tutu waistband. Cropped, fitted, done. Check the size chart on the listing before you order, because wrap tops can run snug through the bust and you want it to land at your natural waist. Too long and it covers the waistband and the whole thing goes lumpy.

sections.heading: Tutu, tights and leg warmers do the costume part
paragraphs: The adult tulle tutu skirt has an elastic waist and enough layers to stand out on its own, no petticoat needed. Pinks shift a lot on a screen. The flat lay version looks hot pink on satin and it photographs blushier in a room, so scroll the customer photos on the listing before you decide it is the wrong color.

Do not skip the soft opaque ballet pink tights. Bare legs with a tutu looks like a dare. Opaque tights make it look on purpose and keep you warm when the trick-or-treat loop runs long. If you are between sizes, size up. Tights that are too short creep down and you will spend the night hiking them up in a hallway.

The ribbed leg warmers are my favorite piece. Scrunch them down so they pool over the top of your flats, like in the photo. That slouch is the whole look. Pulled up tight to the knee they read gym class. They also hide the spot where tights bag at the ankle, which is a small mercy. And yes, they are warm, which matters at a porch full of candy and a door that will not stay shut.

sections.heading: Satin flats and the coffee incident
paragraphs: The satin ballet flats have the ribbon detail and a little elastic strap across the top, which is the part that actually keeps them on your feet. Ballet style flats are thin soled, so they are great for a party and less great for a mile of sidewalk. Add a gel insole if you will be walking a lot.

Now the coffee. I wore this around the house before I shot it, glitter tumbler in hand, and dripped iced coffee straight onto one satin toe. Satin does not forgive. Blot it with a damp cloth, do not rub, and let it dry flat. Lesson learned, lid on, every time. If you are going somewhere with drinks in red cups, consider a spray-on fabric protector the week before. Future you will be grateful.

sections.heading: Hair, makeup and wearing it all again
paragraphs: Keep the beauty simple. A slicked back bun, a pink lip and a little shimmer on the cheeks is plenty. If you want more ballet, wrap a ribbon around the bun. The tulips, candle, lipstick, iced coffee and satin hair bow in the flat lay are styling extras, not part of the costume, and the pumpkin by the door is just my house in October.

After Halloween the tutu goes in a drawer, sure. Everything else keeps working. The wrap top goes over jeans or a slip skirt. The tights go under every winter dress you own. The leg warmers go over sneakers on errand days. If you already have a pink long sleeve top or plain pink flats, start there and only buy the tutu and tights.
